newsitem.title: UK: BP Q2 profit up, plans share buy backs.
newsitem.headline: BP Q2 profit up, plans share buy backs.

text.p: Higher downstream and chemicals results lifted second-quarter profits for British Petroleum Plc, which on Tuesday announced it planned to buy back shares "from time to time".
Profit in the second quarter rose to 740 million pounds ($1.2 billion) from 648 million, exceeding analysts' forecasts.
Shares in BP climbed 26-1/2 pence to 848-1/2 after the results releases and news of the share buy-back plan, which came sooner than industry watchers had expected.
"I believe we can say we have the capacity for additional distribution to shareholders," chief executive John Browne said in a statement.
Meanwhile, operating profit in refining and marketing represented the best second-quarter performance in a decade, BP said. But the group expects refining margins to remain under pressure.
The results in chemicals rose 24 percent due to increased volumes offsetting a weaker overall environment.
Profits in the exploration and production sector were unchanged in dollar terms with an improved operating performance offsetting the negative impact of a lower oil price, BP said.

The oil giant expects higher upstream production in the second half of the year. But oil demand is likely to remain strong, although increasing Iraqi exports "may lead to short term price volatility."
BP raised its interim dividend by 10 percent to 5.5 pence per share. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
